title: What if You Ate The Most Poisonous Animal in the World?
analysis_notes: 9:16 TikTok repost (270x480 source, 30fps). NOT faceless: the creator (green-screened, backwards cap, holding a small lav/mic toward camera) is keyed over full-bleed stock photos for the whole video. No YouTube auto-subs; transcript from faster-whisper small on CPU, corrected against burned-in captions (whisper heard 'murder guppies' / 'Never year' / 'push you in a newspaper' -> captions read 'guppy', 'every year', 'put you in a newspaper'). Description/tags reference the TikTok handle Mndiaye_97, 'Hood nature', 'Not so fun facts'. Contact sheet sampled at 1 fps (60 frames). Very high like ratio (7.6% of views).
title_pattern: 'What if You [did extreme bodily thing] [superlative-ranked object]?' -- second-person hypothetical + superlative ('the Most Poisonous Animal in the World'). Self-insert body-horror question; the answer is a body timeline, so the title promises a play-by-play.

thumbnail.composition: Auto-picked first frame of the vertical video (YouTube shows it pillarboxed with blurred sides). Full-bleed yellow diamond hazard sign with black skull-and-crossbones fills the frame; word 'POISON' huge across lower third, partially occluded by the presenter cut-out bottom-left (so it reads '...OISON'). White rounded-rectangle caption pill top-centre with the title.
thumbnail.text: 'What if You Ate the Most Poisonous Animal on Earth' (black sans-serif on white pill, 3 lines, TikTok native text style)
thumbnail.colours: Saturated warning yellow + pure black iconography, white pill text box, presenter's black tee and red cap strap as small accents.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Universal danger icon (skull) is giant and centred; the human is small, bottom-left, deadpan face -- deadpan human vs. screaming hazard symbol. The animal itself is NOT shown, which keeps the curiosity gap open.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Hazard-sign yellow/black is the most pre-learned 'danger' signal there is and pops in a feed; the question text is the full title so the premise is readable in one glance; a real deadpan face adds personality/trust. Withholding the creature forces the tap.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: This is what would happen if you ate the most poisonous animal in the world. This tiny fish is toxic enough to murk 30 people.
hook.verbatim_5_to_8s: This poison is 1,200 times worse than cyanide.
hook.device: Instant premise restatement (title read aloud at frame 0, no intro) -> reveal of the subject as a 'tiny fish' (small-thing/big-danger contrast) -> two stacked lethality stats with concrete comparators (30 people; 1,200x cyanide). Slang verb 'murk' sets the comedic, irreverent voice in the first 5 s. Visual: hazard-sign background for 3 s, then a hard cut to the actual fish exactly when it is named.

beats.summary: Reads the title verbatim as a second-person hypothetical over a poison hazard sign.
Reveals subject is a tiny fish (pufferfish); kills 30 people; 1,200x worse than cyanide.
First 10 minutes: tingling lips -> numb mouth, drooling -> nausea as body tries to vomit it out. 'First... then... then' sequencing.
Names tetrodotoxin, a neurotoxin that blocks nerve signals to muscles -> explains the creeping paralysis.
30-40 minutes: can't talk, dizziness, 'one hell of a headache'.
'But don't worry, it gets worse.' Ironic reassurance re-hook at ~46% runtime, paired with a background change to a spikier fish.
Toxin reaches respiratory system; trouble breathing, shutting down from the inside.
'Don't bother praying, whoever you're praying to is gonna see you very soon' -- gallows-humour punchline.
Lack of air puts you to sleep; 'no iPhone alarm loud enough to wake you up' (modern-object joke); all within a few hours.
'Fun fact -- really what-the-f*** fact': people eat this fish on purpose as a delicacy (fugu). Turns the hypothetical into a real-world risk.
Safe only if the chef removes the poisonous organs; miss by a little and 'it's curtains'.
A lethal dose fits on a pinhead (shown with tweezers holding a tiny crystal).
'Eating this murder guppy is Russian roulette, and every year someone loses the gamble.' Punchy metaphor, ends abruptly on the last word (loops cleanly).

pacing.rehook_interval_s: ~14 (stat at 3.5, mechanism at 17, 'it gets worse' at 27, joke at 33, twist at 43, pinhead at 53)
pacing.notes: Extremely dense delivery (~4.7 words/s) with almost no pauses; timeline markers ('first 10 minutes', '30-40 minutes', 'a few hours') give the viewer a clock. Visuals change slowly (background every ~7 s) but presenter position jump-cuts every 3-5 s and captions every ~2.8 s keep the eye moving. Each new background lands on a beat change (subject reveal, mechanism, escalation, twist, scale, closer).

techniques_worth_copying: Open by reading the title as a second-person hypothetical at frame 0 -- zero intro, zero channel branding.
Small-thing/big-danger reveal: 'this tiny fish' + two concrete lethality comparisons (people killed, multiple of a famous poison) inside the first 8 s.
Structure the body as a clock-stamped symptom timeline (first 10 min -> 30-40 min -> few hours); each stage is one sentence with a 'then'. Easy to script and inherently escalating.
Name the mechanism once (tetrodotoxin -> blocks nerve signals) mid-video to earn credibility between the gross-out beats.
Ironic-reassurance re-hook at ~45%: 'But don't worry, it gets worse.' Pair with a harsher/spikier visual.
Gallows-humour punchlines with modern everyday references ('no iPhone alarm loud enough') every ~10-15 s.

Late twist that grounds the hypothetical in reality ('people eat this on purpose') at ~73% runtime, then a scale visual (lethal dose on a pinhead) and a metaphor closer ('Russian roulette... someone loses the gamble').
End on the punchline with no CTA so the Short loops.
Background changes only at beat boundaries; in-between motion comes from position jump-cuts and fresh caption cards every ~3 s.
Caption = sentence-level card (not word-by-word karaoke), top third, white with black stroke; occasional second caption mid-frame for the punchline/aside.

code_only_remake_requirements.replace_presenter: No face-cam allowed: substitute a recurring illustrated narrator (SVG character or mascot with 2-4 expressions, small idle bob, mouth flap driven by TTS amplitude) that jumps left/right corners every 3-5 s, or drop the narrator and use a 'you' avatar body silhouette that reacts to each symptom.
code_only_remake_requirements.assets: SVG pufferfish (deflated + inflated + spiky porcupinefish variants), hazard-sign diamond with skull, fugu chrysanthemum plate (radial petal SVG), tweezers + tiny crystal macro scene, simple human head/body silhouette with highlightable zones (lips, mouth, stomach, nerves/muscles, lungs).
code_only_remake_requirements.scenes: ~8 background scenes at 6-8 s each, mapped 1:1 to beats; letterboxed 'photo band' layout (black top band for caption, illustration band middle) is trivial in Remotion.
code_only_remake_requirements.motion: Slow Ken Burns zoom on each background (the original is static -- an easy upgrade), hard cuts on beat changes, quick scale-pop on stat numbers (30 people, 1,200x cyanide), body-silhouette zones lighting up per symptom, a ticking clock/timer chip (10 min -> 30-40 min -> hours) as a persistent HUD element, red pulse/vignette on 'it gets worse'.
code_only_remake_requirements.captions: Sentence-level caption cards (~2.8 s each), bold white sans with black stroke in the upper third, secondary mid-frame card for asides/punchlines; timed from TTS word timestamps.
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Fast TTS (target ~250-280 wpm; Kokoro at speed 1.2-1.3) with deadpan/comedic read; light whoosh on background cuts; no music required (original is voice-only).
code_only_remake_requirements.script: ~270-word original script for 58-60 s: hypothetical premise, 2 stats, 3-stage clock timeline with a mechanism line, ironic re-hook, 2 dark jokes, real-world twist, scale image, metaphor closer. Different animal/toxin, original wording (originality_check must PASS).
